course_description:
Students are assumed to have successfully completed a course on object oriented programming such as CSSE2002, with a good understanding of object oriented principles. Strong programming experience (in any language) will be an advantage. Students are also assumed to have some basic knowledge of computer systems (e.g. from CSSE2010) and mathematics skills including summations, recursions, functions, set theory, and proofs by induction and contradiction.

Course Overview

This course will introduce data structures and algorithms that are important for designing computer programs with performance guarantees and constitute the basis of complex software systems. Broadly speaking, this course will teach you to think - and to solve problems - like a computer scientist. The course will also cover a set of analytical techniques that are fundamental for advanced studies in theoretical computer science.

Changes to this offering

AI Usage Expectations

While AI tools may be used in this course, AI is not required nor is encouraged. Students will receive guidance on acceptable AI use, attribution or disclosure. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

course_aims: This course will build an understanding of how the architecture of a computer impacts the construction of programs and how data structures and algorithms can be constructed to efficiently perform desired functionality. The goal of this course is to build enough understanding of data structures and associated algorithms so that an appropriate set can be selected in the design of new software. The students should develop an understanding of:

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the principles of data structures - Understand the internal workings of fundamental data structures and algorithms
Understand the principles of data structures - Determine the running time and memory space usage of common algorithms.
Develop algorithmic solutions - Analyse the performance of fundamental data structures and algorithms
Develop algorithmic solutions - Adapt or invent new algorithms and data structures for software engineering problems.
Develop algorithmic solutions - Select and justify appropriate combinations of data structures and algorithms to solve software engineering problems.
Develop algorithmic solutions - Communicate the efficiency and correctness of identified solutions

assessment_details.title: Problem Sets
assessment_details.task_description: Problems are designed to consolidate the knowledge of the course material, demonstrate your ability to understand data structures, solve simple algorithmic problems, compute the time and space complexity of algorithms, optimize their computational complexity, or debug existing data structures. These activities are designed to keep students engaged with the week-by-week teaching material. The best 8 out of 10 submissions will be used to calculate a student's mark, with each submission weighted equally. Each problem will be accompanied by a detailed specification sheet uploaded to Blackboard. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. See additional assessment information below for more information. Read full task description Hide full task description

The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.

The assessment will be submitted online via the Gradescope platform. Detailed instructions will be provided in the task specification.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Because only the best 8 out of 10 problem sets will contribute to the mark for this assessment item and results/answers are released soon after the due date, no extensions are permitted.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
Because the results/answers are released soon after the due date, and only the best 8 out of 10 will contribute to the mark for this assessment item, a 100% penalty will be applied to late submissions. This has been approved by the Associate Dean (Academic).
